This section is for anyone adding or editing pages. Read it before touching anything.

Admonitions Admonitions are callout boxes for things that need to stand out. Keep them short and punchy - one or two sentences max. Here are all the available types: note This is a note. Use it for neutral extra context that's helpful but not critical. Tag: :::note tip This is a tip. Use it for shortcuts, recommendations, or things that make life easier. Tag: :::tip info This is an info box. Use it for background context the reader might not know. Tag: :::info caution This is a caution. Use it for things that are easy to get wrong or miss. Also used as a placeholder marker for screenshots that still need to be added. Tag: :::caution warning This is a warning. Use it for things that can actually break something if ignored. Tag: :::warning danger This is danger. Use it sparingly - only for things with serious consequences. Tag: :::danger For screenshot placeholders specifically, the convention is: :::caution Put an image of X here ::: Don't remove these - they mark where screenshots still need to go. When you have the screenshot, replace the whole block with a standard image tag.

Page Structure Every page file is .mdx (not .md) so React components work inline. The frontmatter at the top sets the sidebar position and title: --- sidebar_position: 2 title: My Page --- To use any of the style components, import them at the top of the file right after the frontmatter block: import { SectionBanner, SubSectionBanner, GaugeHeader, SectionTab } from '@site/src/components/XenoMarkers';

Using the Style Components Most of the time you just need ## headings - they automatically get the SectionBanner style with no import required: ## My Section Use the explicit components when you need something the auto-style can't do, like a tab label above a banner, a named sub-section break, or a gauge bar with a right-side value: <SectionTab>Optional</SectionTab> <SectionBanner>My Section</SectionBanner> <SubSectionBanner>Named Break</SubSectionBanner> <GaugeHeader value="3/3">Progress Header</GaugeHeader>

Sizing Overrides Every component accepts a size prop that sets its font-size. Because all internal dimensions (padding, taper depth, margins) use em units, everything scales proportionally - you only need to change one value: <SectionBanner size="0.8rem">Smaller than default</SectionBanner> <SectionBanner size="1.5rem">Bigger than default</SectionBanner> <GaugeHeader size="1rem" value="done">Larger gauge</GaugeHeader> Default sizes: SectionTab → 0.72rem, SectionBanner → 1rem, SubSectionBanner → 1.25rem, GaugeHeader → 0.78rem.

ToC and Components The table of contents only picks up markdown ## headings - JSX components are invisible to it. If a section using an explicit component also needs a ToC entry, add a ## heading immediately before it: ## My Section <SectionBanner>My Section</SectionBanner> The CSS collapses the ## heading visually (so the component shows instead) while keeping the anchor alive for the ToC link.

Images and Assets Static images go in static/img/. In markdown prose, use the path as-is: ![alt text](/img/something.png) Inside a React component or JSX, always use useBaseUrl or the path will break in production: import useBaseUrl from '@docusaurus/useBaseUrl'; const src = useBaseUrl('/img/something.png');
Colors Never hardcode hex or rgb values anywhere in CSS or JSX. Always reference the CSS variables defined in src/css/custom.css. The full palette is in the color swatches above.

Unity Icons Small inline icons that match the Unity editor's own file-type indicators. Use them next to any mention of a specific Unity asset type so readers can visually identify the file they're looking for. Import from UnityIcon: import { SceneIcon, PrefabIcon, ModelIcon, PrefabModelIcon, PrefabVariantIcon, UnityPackageIcon, UnityPackage } from '@site/src/components/UnityIcon'; Available icons: <SceneIcon /> <PrefabIcon /> <ModelIcon /> <PrefabModelIcon /> <PrefabVariantIcon /> <UnityPackageIcon /> All icon components accept an optional size prop (number, pixels). Default is 16. Double-click the scene file <SceneIcon /> to open it. Drag the prefab <PrefabIcon /> into the Hierarchy. <UnityPackage /> is a special badge that combines the .unitypackage filename and icon into a styled inline element that looks like a code span: Save your .unitypackage file somewhere you can find it. Save your <UnityPackage /> file somewhere you can find it. Use <UnityPackage /> wherever you'd otherwise write `.unitypackage` <UnityPackageIcon /> — it's the same thing in one tag.
A reference for errors you're likely to run into when uploading or using avatars.

Cause: The selected object doesn't have a VRC Avatar Descriptor component, or no object is selected in the Builder tab. Fix: Select the root GameObject of your avatar in the scene, then open the SDK Builder tab again. Make sure a VRC Avatar Descriptor is attached to that object.

Cause: Often a script compilation error somewhere in the project that prevents Unity from building. Fix: Check the Unity Console (Window → General → Console) for any red errors. Fix all script errors before trying to upload. If errors are in third-party packages, try reimporting them via the Creator Companion.

Cause: The upload may have succeeded but the avatar is still processing on VRChat's servers, or you're looking in the wrong place. Fix: Wait a few minutes and check My Avatars in the VRChat menu. Make sure you're logged into the same VRChat account in-game as you used for the upload. If it still doesn't appear, check the VRChat Content Manager in the SDK to confirm the upload completed.

documents.t: Cause: The Quest and PC versions have different Pipeline IDs and aren't linked. Fix: See the Quest version linking steps in the Uploading guide. info Don't see your error here? More entries will be added over time. Feel free to reach out if you're stuck.

documents.t: If you've changed something on your avatar - or updated your packages - you'll need to re-upload for those changes to actually show up in VRChat. It's basically the same process as the first upload. info Re-uploading overwrites the existing version of your avatar. No duplicates - it just updates the same one in your list.

Any time you've changed something in Unity that you want to see in VRChat. For example: You updated a package (like GoGoLoco or VRCFury) You swapped out a texture or material You adjusted a setting on the avatar You made any other edit inside the Unity project Just updating packages in VCC is not enough on its own - you always need to re-upload after.
documents.s: When do you need to re-upload?

documents.t: Open your project in Unity through the Creator Companion. Make sure your avatar is in the scene. If it isn't, find it in the Project window and drag it into the Hierarchy. Click VRChat SDK in the top menu bar, then Show Control Panel. Go to the Builder tab and confirm your avatar is selected in the dropdown. Check for any red errors - fix those before continuing. Click Build & Publish for Windows. Wait for Unity to finish building. This can take a few minutes. Done - your avatar in VRChat will now reflect the changes. tip You don't need to re-enter the name or description. VRChat remembers those from the first upload since you're updating, not creating a new one.

If your avatar has a Quest version, you'll need to re-upload that separately too. Once you've done the steps above, repeat them and click Build & Publish for Android instead of Windows. The Quest and PC versions are linked by their shared ID so you don't need to go through the ID-linking process again - that only has to be done once on first upload.
To get the avatar into Unity you need to import a Unity Package - a .unitypackage file that contains the model, textures, animations, and everything else the avatar needs.
Open the Creator Companion and go to the Projects tab. Click Open Project next to your project. Unity will launch, which can take a minute or two. info Unity is slow to open. Just let it load.
documents.s: Step 1 - Open your project in Unity

documents.t: You should have a .unitypackage file from your avatar download, named something like Lucario ReUnited VRC.unitypackage. ⚠️Put a screenshot of the right-click menu here Right-click Menu tip Not sure where it is? Check your Downloads folder, or wherever you saved it after downloading.
There are three ways to do this - pick whichever works for you:

Option A - Right-click the Assets folder The Project window is the panel at the bottom of Unity that shows all your project files. Inside it you'll see a folder called Assets in the left sidebar. warning Project window vs Hierarchy These two panels are easy to mix up. The Hierarchy (left side of the screen) shows the objects in your current scene. The Project window (bottom) shows your files on disk. You want the Project window for this step. Right-click the Assets folder. Hover over Import Package. Click Custom Package.... Find your .unitypackage file in the file browser and select it. ▶Video coming soon Right-click Menu
documents.s: Option A - Right-click the Assets folder

documents.t: Option B - Drag and drop Open the folder where your .unitypackage file is saved. Drag the file on top of the Project window in Unity. Hold until the cursor changes, then let go. ▶Video coming soon Drag and Drop

Option C - Double-click the file Find the .unitypackage file in your file explorer. Double-click the .unitypackage. If Unity is open it will pick it up automatically. ▶Video coming soon Double-click Import Whichever method you used, Unity will show a list of everything in the package. Leave everything checked and click Import. caution Put an image of the Import dialog here Wait for the progress bar in the bottom-right corner to finish before doing anything else. info FBX import warnings may appear in the Console after importing. As long as the text is yellow and not red, they are safe to ignore.

Once the import finishes, navigate to this folder in the Project window: Assets / Monado_Art / Lucario ReUnited VRC / You may also notice a _MekenoTools folder in your Assets. It's a dependency that came with the avatar - just leave it alone, you don't need to touch it. Inside you'll find: The Scene - Double-click to open it. If you're new to Unity this is the easiest starting point since the avatar is already set up inside it. The Prefab - Drag it from the Project window into the Hierarchy to add it to your scene. The included scene has both prefabs placed in it side by side, so opening it first is a good way to see what each one looks like. There are two versions: Lucario ReUnited PC Prefab - the base version, with the Sir Aaron outfit and mohawk hair on by default. Lucario ReUnited PC Lite Prefab - same but with a few things removed to hit a better performance rank. Good pick if you want to be easier on lower-end PCs. caution Put an image of the Project window showing the folder and files here
documents.s: Step 4 - Find the scene and prefab

documents.t: warning I know, you're probably very excited to start customizing the avatar right now! - but hold off for just a bit! Do a clean upload first to make sure everything is working correctly before you start making changes. It's much easier to spot problems on a fresh import than after you've already modified things. Head to Uploading to get it into VRChat first.
To get an avatar into VRChat, you'll need to install a few things first. This page walks you through all of it step by step - no prior experience needed.​

warning Your VRChat account needs to have a trust rank of New User or above in order to be able to upload avatars! If you just made your VRChat account you will need to play the game or afk in order to increase it from Visitor. Positive interactions with people (such as not getting blocked or getting friend requests) will allow you to gain trust rank faster, alternatively you can pay for VRC+ and gain New User rank immediately! Trust Ranks

The VRChat Creator Companion (usually just called VCC) is a free program made by VRChat. Think of it as a control panel that helps you set up everything else. You install it once and it handles the rest. Go to vrchat.com and log in with your VRChat account. Click Downloads from the top menu. Download the Creator Companion and run the installer like you would any other program. When you open it for the first time, it will ask you to sign in with your VRChat account. Go ahead and do that. info If it asks for a verification code after signing in, check your email - VRChat sends one for security.

Unity is the program that actually lets you upload the avatar. VCC will prompt you to install it automatically, so you don't need to go hunting for the right version yourself. Open the Creator Companion. If Unity isn't installed yet, VCC will show a message asking you to install it. Click Install Unity. This opens a program called Unity Hub - it's just a launcher that manages Unity for you. Follow the prompts to finish installing. During setup, you'll be asked to create a free Unity account and activate a Personal license. This is completely free and just lets you use Unity. warning Don't install Unity yourself If you go to the Unity website and download it manually, you'll probably get the wrong version. VRChat is very picky about which version it supports - always let VCC install it for you. caution Already have Unity installed? You might have the wrong version. If you haven't updated VCC or Unity in a while, you may have Unity 2019 installed instead of the required Unity 2022. Using the wrong version will cause your project to break. To fix this: First, make sure your Creator Companion itself is up to date - check for updates and install them if available. Open the Creator Companion and go to Settings in the bottom-left corner. Click the General tab. If you see a pop-up or banner that says something like "No Recommended Version Yet" or shows an outdated Unity version, click Install Now. Wait for Unity Hub to finish installing the correct version. Once Unity 2022 is installed, you're good to continue.

A "project" is just a folder on your computer where all your avatar files will live. You create and manage it through the Creator Companion. Open the Creator Companion and click Projects in the sidebar on the left. Click the blue Create New Project button in the top right. From the template list, select "Unity 2022 Avatar Project". Give your project a name and choose where to save it. tip Choose a sensible save location By default, VCC might try to save it inside a hidden system folder (AppData). It's better to save it somewhere easy to find, like Documents\VRChat Projects\ or similar. Click Create and wait for it to finish. This might take a minute or two.

Before you can install anything, VCC needs to know where to find these packages. Click Add to VCC on each card below. Once you've clicked all four, a message will appear at the bottom telling you what to do next. Mandatory Dependencies VRCFury Automatically sets up complex avatar features so you don't have to do it manually. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://vcc.vrcfury.com Poiyomi Toon The shader used for the avatar's materials. Without it, the avatar will appear completely pink. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://poiyomi.github.io/vpm/index.json Optional - but heavily recommended ⚠️ These packages are not strictly required, but pay close attention during the upload process if you skip them - missing packages will produce errors and the upload will fail. GoGoLoco Adds movement options like sitting and laying down anywhere in VRChat. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://Spokeek.github.io/goloco/index.json ADJerry's Face Tracking Templates Adds face tracking support to the avatar. Add to VCC Didn't work? Go to Settings > Packages > Add Repository and paste: https://Adjerry91.github.io/VRCFaceTracking-Templates/index.json info You only need to do this once per package, ever. Once a source is added to VCC, it stays there for all future projects too.
documents.s: Step 4 - Add the package sources to VCC

documents.t: Now that VCC knows where the packages are, you need to actually install them into your project. This is the step that puts them in your Unity project and makes them usable. Open the Creator Companion and click Projects in the sidebar on the left. Find your project in the list and click Manage Project. You'll see a list of packages. Find each of the following and click the button next to them: VRCFury GoGoLoco VRCFT - Jerry's Templates Poiyomi Toon - Make sure you pick Toon, not Pro. Pro is the paid version - if you haven't purchased it, installing Pro will not work correctly. Wait for VCC to finish installing each one - it may take a moment. info You'll know it worked when the version box changes from none to a version number (e.g. 1.2.3), and the button changes to .
documents.s: Step 5 - Install the packages into your project

documents.t: Once everything is installed, head to Uploading to get your avatar into VRChat.

tip Already know Unity? If you've used Unity before and feel comfortable navigating it, feel free to skip straight to Uploading. When you open your project for the first time, Unity can look pretty overwhelming. There are panels everywhere and none of it is obvious. This page breaks down what each part of the screen does so you're not flying blind.

When Unity first opens, you'll see something like this: Unity Editor Layout Each section is its own panel, and you can resize or rearrange them. Don't worry if yours looks slightly different - Unity lets you move things around.

Where: Top-left panel. Hierarchy Panel The Hierarchy is a list of everything that exists in your current scene. Think of it like a folder tree - objects can be nested inside other objects. For avatar work, this is where you'll find your avatar. It will usually appear as a single entry that you can click the arrow next to expand and see all its parts (bones, meshes, etc.). When you click something in the Hierarchy, it gets selected and its details show up in the Inspector on the right. Hierarchy - Inspector Link

Where: Right-side panel. Inspector Panel The Inspector shows you the details of whatever you have selected. If you click on your avatar in the Hierarchy, the Inspector will show all the components attached to it - things like the Avatar Descriptor (which tells VRChat this is an avatar) and any other settings. You'll interact with the Inspector a lot when following guides, since most settings are changed here. info If you click somewhere and the Inspector goes blank or shows something unexpected, you probably just accidentally selected the wrong thing. Go back to the Hierarchy and click what you actually wanted.

Where: Large panel in the center. Scene View The Scene View is a 3D viewport where you can see and move around your avatar visually. You can think of it like a free camera flying around your scene. Basic controls: Right-click + drag - Rotate the camera Right-click + WASD - Fly through the scene (hold right-click, then move with WASD) Right-click + Q/E - Move the camera down/up while flying Middle-click + drag - Pan the camera Scroll wheel - Zoom in/out Press F (with something selected) - Focus the camera on that object caution TODO Mention scroll speed and shift to speed up flying Scene View Navigation For uploading, you don't really need to move things around in the Scene View - just knowing how to navigate it is enough.

Where: Usually tabbed behind the Scene View (click the "Game" tab to switch). Game View The Game View shows what the camera inside the scene sees - basically a preview of what things would look like in-game. For avatar uploading you won't use this much.

Where: Bottom panel. Project Window The Project window is your file browser. It shows all the files that make up your project - textures, materials, scripts, prefabs, and so on. Think of it like File Explorer, but only showing the contents of your project folder. When you import your avatar files, they'll appear here. You can double-click folders to open them, and drag files from the Project window into the Hierarchy to add them to your scene. Project - Hierarchy Drag

Where: Usually tabbed next to the Project window (click "Console" to switch). Console The Console shows messages from Unity - information, warnings, and errors. White messages - General info, usually safe to ignore. Yellow messages - Warnings. Often harmless, but worth noting. Red messages - Errors. These mean something is actually wrong and usually need to be fixed before you can upload. If your upload fails or something breaks, the Console is the first place to check. tip If you see a wall of red errors when you first open your project, don't panic. Make sure all four packages from the Installation step are properly installed - missing packages are the most common cause.

Where: Very top of the window. Toolbar The row of menus across the top (File, Edit, Assets, GameObject, Component, VRChat SDK, Window, Help) works like any other program. The one you'll use most is VRChat SDK, which is where you open the upload panel.
Now that you know your way around, head to Uploading to get your avatar into VRChat.

This page covers how to upload your avatar using the VRChat SDK inside Unity. Make sure you've completed the Installation steps before continuing. Outfits and other customization options are covered in the Customizing section.

In Unity, go to the top menu bar and click: VRChat SDK → Show Control Panel caution Put an image of where to find it This opens the SDK window. If you don't see this menu, the SDK probably isn't installed correctly - go back to the Creator Companion and make sure the VRChat SDK package is added to your project.

In the SDK window, go to the Authentication tab and sign in with your VRChat account. tip Sign in with your email address, not your username. Username login tends not to work reliably in the SDK. note You may be prompted for a two-factor authentication code. Check your email.

Switch to the Builder tab at the top of the SDK window. In the Selected Avatar dropdown, choose your avatar. The SDK will run a few checks on your avatar. Fix any errors shown in red before continuing. Warnings (yellow) are usually safe to ignore.

Fill in the Avatar Name and give it a Thumbnail. Description and tags are entirely optional. Scroll down in the Builder tab. Make sure Build & Publish your Avatar Online is selected as the "Build Type" and "Windows" is selected in the "Platform" dropdown. Wait for Unity to build the avatar. Depending on how many components you have added this can take a few minutes. If successful you will see a message saying "Build Successful" in green text. Once finished, your avatar will appear in VRChat under My Avatars.

If you want to upload a Mobile compatible version, you need to link it to the same pipeline ID as the PC version so they're uploaded onto the same avatar. Find the prefab for the Mobile version of the avatar and drag it into the hierarchy, add the same additions as you did on the PC version. In the SDK's Content Manager tab, find your uploaded PC avatar and click Copy ID. In your scene, select the root object of the Quest avatar. Find the Pipeline Manager component on it. Paste the copied ID into the Blueprint ID field and click Attach. Now repeat the upload steps above using Build & Publish Your Avatar Online with "Android" selected in the "Platform" dropdown. caution If the mobile avatar is not uploaded onto the same Blueprint ID as the PCVR version they will be treated as two entirely different avatar uploads. This means that if you are on PCVR your Quest standalone friends wont see your avatar and vice-versa.
If something goes wrong during the upload, check the Troubleshooting page for common errors and fixes.
If the upload went through, nice work! If you want to start customizing the avatar - outfits, accessories, that sort of thing - head over to the Customizing section.
